title: Caching: exact, semantic & embedding caches
summary: Don't pay twice for the same answer. An **exact cache** answers identical requests for free, shared by every server process in Redis and normalized so case and punctuation don't matter. A **semantic cache** reuses answers to paraphrases, which is where the danger lives: near-misses that differ in one detail look identical to an embedding model. The module measures that danger, guards against it, chooses the threshold from labelled pairs, compares four stores, and replays real support traffic through every kind of cache.
learn: **Exact caches**: set_llm_cache, what the key contains, Redis shared by every process, normalized keys
**Semantic caches**: lookup by meaning, what an entry stores, and the near-miss trap
**Guards**: an entity guard, never-cache rules, versions and TTLs, scopes
**The threshold from data**, and **stores** compared: memory, SQLite, Redis Vector Sets, pgvector
**In production**: what to cache (embeddings too), provider prompt caching, stampedes, warm-up, metrics
flow:
question ─→ personal or time-sensitive? ──yes──→ model (never cached)
   └─→ exact key (normalized) ──hit──→ answer
   └─→ embed ─→ nearest in scope (Redis Vector Sets) ─→ similarity ≥ 0.75? same entities? same versions? not expired?
         ──yes──→ answer        ──no──→ model ─→ store if cacheable

path.title: Production path: a guarded semantic cache in Redis
path.summary: Questions that are personal or time-sensitive never touch the cache. Everything else is looked up by meaning in Redis Vector Sets, within its scope, and an answer is reused only above the measured threshold, with the same entities and versions, before its TTL. Identical questions in flight share one model call.

steps.title: Rules
steps.explain: cacheable() refuses personal questions (order ids, "my order"), time-sensitive ones and refusals or errors; lookup() skips the same questions.
production: Every new kind of personal question is a rule here before it's a bug report.

steps.title: Guard
steps.explain: entities() extracts ids, numbers, dates, places, menu items and cafés; a cached answer is reused only when they match. Entries carry model, prompt and index versions and a TTL.
production: Bump the index version on re-ingestion: every answer built on the old documents retires.

steps.title: Store
steps.explain: RedisVectorStore keeps vectors in a Vector Set (VADD/VSIM with a scope FILTER) and payloads in hashes with their own TTL: shared by every process.
production: Watch hit rate and false-hit rate on a dashboard; sample hits for review.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
Paraphrases, repeats and near-misses (another drink, city, number or order id) through five caches.

| | hit rate | false hits | model calls | tokens | latency p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no cache | 0% | 0 | 28 | 3,985 | 2.0 s |
| exact | 14% | 0 | 24 | 3,416 | 2.2 s |
| exact, normalized | 21% | 0 | 22 | 3,119 | 2.4 s |
| semantic, unguarded | 61% | 4 | 11 | 1,570 | 0.007 s |
| **semantic, guarded (production)** | **43%** | **0** | **16** | **2,304** | **0.9 s** |

The unguarded semantic cache looked best on every cost number and gave four customers someone else's answer: Pune got Mumbai's delivery time (similarity 0.84), a refund after 20 days got the answer for 10 days (0.90), ₹1,300 got the points for ₹500 (0.89), and NC-1003 got NC-1002's cancellation answer (0.97). The guards (never caching order questions, and requiring the same numbers, places and products) removed all four for 18 fewer points of hit rate, and still saved 12 of 28 model calls. Normalizing exact keys added hits with no risk. The threshold (0.75) came from labelled pairs: on its own no threshold separated paraphrases from near-misses, and with the entity guard none of the near-misses hit.
production: Re-run with real traffic samples before changing the threshold or the embedding model.
